preamble: Vocalization of a syllable-final [p] to the high back vowel [u] (realized as the offglide of a diphthong) is rare. The clearest case is Spanish, where Latin coda p in semi-learned words became the glide u: captīvus > cautivo 'captive', baptīzāre > bautizar 'to baptize'. Inherited words normally show assimilation instead (septem > siete), and forms such as caudillo < capitellum passed through a voiced stage (Old Spanish cabdiello), so they belong under b_to_u.

examples.note: Semi-learned; the inherited outcome is the now-rare cativo, with assimilation of pt.
Via older Spanish baptizar; the coda labial became the offglide of /au/.
Semi-learned, from older baptismo; the same root and outcome as bautizar.

sources: Penny, R. (2002). A History of the Spanish Language (2nd ed.). Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511992827
